name: Interleukin-1 Receptor-Associated Kinase 4 Deficiency

criteria.description: Recurrent invasive bacterial infections, especially caused by Streptococcus pneumoniae and Staphylococcus aureus
Demonstrated impaired Toll-like receptor (TLR) signaling in functional assays
Identification of biallelic pathogenic mutations in the IRAK4 gene by genetic testing
Absent or low inflammatory response (e.g., low C-reactive protein) during bacterial infections
Normal adaptive immune function (normal immunoglobulin levels and lymphocyte subsets)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of recurrent invasive bacterial infections plus either impaired TLR signaling or biallelic pathogenic IRAK4 mutations
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Functional testing of TLR signaling and genetic confirmation are critical for diagnosis.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Impaired inflammatory response to bacterial infections
pathognomonic.notes: Low or absent fever and low acute phase reactants

occasional.notes: Fever may be absent or delayed despite infection
Poor growth in infancy and early childhood

laboratory: Low or absent C-reactive protein and other acute phase reactants during bacterial infections
Normal immunoglobulin levels and lymphocyte subsets
Impaired cytokine production in response to TLR agonists
imaging: Radiographic evidence of pneumonia or osteomyelitis
MRI or CT may show complications of meningitis
genetic: Biallelic pathogenic variants in IRAK4 gene confirmed by sequencing
other: Functional assays demonstrating defective TLR signaling pathways

distinguishingFeatures: Similar clinical phenotype but caused by MYD88 mutations
May have overlapping TLR signaling defects
Recurrent bacterial and fungal infections with granuloma formation
Positive nitroblue tetrazolium test or dihydrorhodamine assay
Other genetic defects affecting TLR pathway

redFlags: Recurrent invasive bacterial infections in infancy or early childhood
Severe infections with low or absent fever and inflammatory markers
Family history of early severe bacterial infections or consanguinity
references: Picard C, et al. IRAK-4 deficiency: clinical, immunological, and genetic features. Immunol Rev. 2010; 234(1): 199-208.
Ku CL, et al. IRAK-4 and MyD88 deficiency in human patients with recurrent bacterial infections. Science. 2007; 317(5834): 1054-1057.
Medvedev AE. Toll-like receptor polymorphisms, inflammatory and infectious diseases, allergies, and cancer. J Interferon Cytokine Res. 2013; 33(9): 467-484.
